zXo84tbA_ZI.one_line: Zuhd as putting true price tags on worldly things and wara' as choosing the morally safer path, with sayings of the early generations.
zXo84tbA_ZI.summary: He introduces zuhd and wara' as two of four outward qualities, with haya and adab, that make a person live well, and quotes the early generations on their worth above extra prayer and fasting. Zuhd is not owning nothing; it is being more confident in what is with Allah than in what is in your own hand. We constantly assign value to possessions, relationships and status, and the pain of losing them shows how much. Zuhd means removing false price tags and seeing worldly things at their real worth, so the heart holds only to what is valuable, above all Allah and His commands. He draws on the Prophet's warnings that he feared worldly competition for his followers more than poverty, the dead goat kid that is worth more than the whole world to Allah, and Abu Hazim's reply to the caliph that people hate death because they built up their worldly life and ruined their hereafter. Detachment also brings freedom: a person whom nothing can be held over cannot be pressured to compromise. Wara' is moral caution between halal, haram and the doubtful. It requires knowledge, since the scholar's job is to find well-founded ease while the individual's job is to choose what is safer, and ignorance turns caution into needless hardship. He closes with Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf weeping over Mus'ab's shroud and urges listeners to detach and choose safely.

outline.heading: Opening
Introducing zuhd and wara'
outline.gist: The English terms sound awkward, but these concepts are simple and come from the early scholars' books on softening the heart.

outline.heading: Haya, adab, zuhd and wara' as the outward domains
outline.gist: A saying holds that whoever combines modesty, manners, asceticism and caution lives well; these are the outer counterparts of inner work on self-value and humility.

outline.heading: The early generations on zuhd and wara'
outline.gist: Salman, Hasan al-Basri, Abu Waqid al-Laythi and Ibn al-Mubarak praise caution and detachment above extra worship as the strongest aid to seeking the hereafter.

outline.heading: Zuhd: trusting what is in Allah's hand more than yours
outline.gist: Abu Muslim al-Khawlani's definition; the problem is building attachment to house, relationships and status.

outline.heading: We assign value to things without noticing
outline.gist: The distress we feel when something is lost or threatened reveals how much value we had given it.

outline.heading: Zuhd as correct price tags, not poverty
outline.gist: You can own a good car and house; zuhd means it does not live in your heart and its loss would not make you miserable.

outline.heading: The delusion of the dunya
outline.gist: Being deceived about wealth, health or position harms a person; seeing things at their real value stops the heart investing in the cheap.

outline.heading: Holding on to what is truly valuable
outline.gist: Zuhd lets you magnify Allah and His commands and rites, because you finally see where real value lies.

outline.heading: The Prophet's pledge: a rider's provision
outline.gist: Some companions pledged to take from the world only what a traveller carries for the journey.

outline.heading: Abu Hazim and the caliph: why we hate death
outline.gist: Sulayman ibn Abd al-Malik asked why people love the world and hate death; Abu Hazim answered that they built their dunya and ruined their akhirah, so they dread moving from the built to the ruined.

outline.heading: Take what you need; attachments give others a hold on you
outline.gist: Provide well for your family but keep wealth off your heart; whoever needs his job, mortgage and school fees can be pressured to compromise.

outline.heading: The freedom of the unattached
outline.gist: No one could pressure Abu Hanifah, Malik, al-Shafi'i or Ahmad because nothing worldly held them.

outline.heading: The wealth of Bahrain: it is not poverty I fear for you
outline.gist: When the Ansar gathered hoping for a share, the Prophet said he feared they would compete for the world and be destroyed as earlier nations were.

outline.heading: The dead goat kid
outline.gist: No one would buy a dead deformed kid even for a dirham; the world is more worthless to Allah than that.

outline.heading: Wara': magnifying halal and haram
outline.gist: Wara' is taking the lawful and unlawful seriously; be cautious and you will be the most devoted of worshippers.

outline.heading: Wara' requires knowledge and is not giving up ambition
outline.gist: Caution can be misread as abandoning ambition; love of the world is the root of every sin, but people still need ambition guided by knowledge.

outline.heading: Halal, haram and the doubtful in between
outline.gist: Whoever avoids doubtful matters protects his religion and honour; the cautious person leaves what is unclear to avoid sin.

outline.heading: The scholar offers ease, you choose safety
outline.gist: A scholar's job is to find well-evidenced flexibility; the individual's job is to take the safer option, like a shepherd keeping away from the king's land.

outline.heading: Ibn Qutaybah on false piety
outline.gist: Turning away in feigned modesty when body parts are mentioned is not wara'; the sin is backbiting, false speech and lying.

outline.heading: Moral frugality: never compromising your positions
outline.gist: When the right is unclear, choose the safer path; but without knowledge caution makes life needlessly hard for you and those around you.

outline.heading: Umar: whenever you desire something, do you buy it?
outline.gist: Umar rebuked a man for buying meat simply because he craved it, teaching restraint over every appetite.

outline.heading: Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf weeping over Mus'ab's shroud
outline.gist: Breaking his fast, he wept remembering that Mus'ab left the world with a cloth too short to cover him, fearing his own rewards had been hastened in this life.

outline.heading: Detach and make the safer choices
outline.gist: Enjoy what you have but do not attach to it, and keep your outward moral choices as close to the ideal as possible.

outline.heading: Outro

ayv5VWt7f3o.title: Ramadan 2025, Night 27: Seventh Night of Tahajjud
ayv5VWt7f3o.one_line: The last movements of the prayer, then the 27th night as a night of pardon: Allah erases sins for those who pardon others.
ayv5VWt7f3o.summary: The twenty-seventh night has two reminders. The first completes the sheikh's nightly walk through the movements of the prayer, in which every physical movement mirrors a change in the soul. He reaches the final positions: the sitting between the two prostrations, where the Prophet would repeat his plea for forgiveness and ask for mercy, wellbeing, pardon, guidance, provision and mending, and then the final sitting, where the worshipper greets Allah, sends peace on His righteous servants, bears witness to His oneness and sends blessings on the Prophet. The second reminder is about pardon. On this night Allah does more than forgive: He can erase a sin altogether. The sheikh paints a scene from the Day of Judgment in which a person turns to the date of a sin in his book, cannot find it and wonders if he has the date wrong, and Allah tells him only the two of them knew of it, and soon only Allah will. The way to earn that pardon is to pardon others, as Umar did when he released people from whatever he held against them. The first pardon is hard, he admits, but after it each one gets easier and lifts a weight off you. He asks everyone to pardon those who insulted them, worked against them or took from them.

outline.heading: Interlude
The last movements: each one mirrors a change in the soul
outline.gist: He returns to the series he has built over the past nights, in which every physical movement of the prayer mirrors a spiritual transformation, and turns to the final movements.

outline.heading: The sitting between the prostrations: asking forgiveness
outline.gist: Between the two prostrations the Prophet would repeat 'My Lord, forgive me' and ask for forgiveness, mercy, wellbeing, pardon, guidance, provision and mending.

outline.heading: The final sitting: addressing Allah with greetings
outline.gist: In the tashahhud the worshipper speaks to Allah directly, opening with greetings that belong to Him alone.

outline.heading: Peace on the righteous, the testimony of oneness and blessings on the Prophet
outline.gist: The sitting continues with peace on Allah's righteous servants, the testimony of tawhid and the prayer for blessings on the Prophet, where he asks people to stay focused and present.

outline.heading: Interlude
Pardon on this night: a sin deleted, not just forgiven
outline.gist: Allah, who pardons, can do more than forgive tonight: He can remove a mistake from your book, so that when you turn to its date on the Day of Judgment you cannot find it and wonder if you have the date wrong.

outline.heading: Only you and Allah knew, and soon only He will
outline.gist: You search back and ask whether it was forgiven instead, and Allah tells you that only the two of you knew of it, and by the time He is done only He will remember.

outline.heading: Pardon others as Umar did, and it gets easier
outline.gist: Umar released people that night from whatever he held against them. The first pardon is hard, but once you reach deep inside, let it go and never speak of it again, it becomes easier and lifts a burden off you; grant it to everyone who insulted you, worked against you or took from you.

outline.heading: Interlude
Outro

CKIs4Nkqebo.title: Ramadan 2025, Night 25: Fifth Night of Tahajjud
CKIs4Nkqebo.one_line: Bowing, rising and prostrating explained: magnifying Allah, thanking Him upright, and pouring out hopes in sujud, with the story of Rabi'ah ibn Ka'b.
CKIs4Nkqebo.summary: On the twenty-fifth night of Ramadan 2025 the sheikh continues his nightly walk through the movements of the prayer, where each physical form mirrors something in the soul. In the first reminder he explains bowing: the Prophet forbade reciting Quran in ruku and made it the place to magnify the Lord, offering his hearing, sight, mind and bones to Allah in humility. Rising from ruku is thanks. No one can thank Allah enough, so you thank Him standing upright, the way a guest who enters a king's court well dressed shows the king's generosity was well placed. He asks people to hold one specific blessing in mind as they praise. He tells how Rabi'ah ibn Ka'b woke in the night to hear the Prophet glorifying and praising at length, and how, offered anything he wished, he asked for the Prophet's company in Paradise and was told to help with many prostrations. In the second reminder he says glorifying Allah adds nothing to Him; it trains the worshipper not to object to His decree when life turns hard. Prostration is for dua: record your hopes there even if life later pulls you elsewhere, and trust that Allah promised to respond, whether by removing a harm, giving something better, giving later, or saving it for when you need it most.

outline.heading: Interlude
Every movement of prayer mirrors the spirit
outline.gist: Each act of worship in Islam has a physical form that mirrors a spiritual meaning, so it matters to understand why each movement is done the way it is.

outline.heading: Ruku is for magnifying the Lord
outline.gist: The Prophet forbade reciting Quran while bowing or prostrating and taught that ruku is where the Lord is glorified, with words such as Subhana Rabbiya al-Azim.

outline.heading: The ruku dua: hearing, sight and bones humbled
outline.gist: In the Prophet's dua in ruku the whole person bows: hearing, sight, mind, bones and sinews humbled to Allah, while the tongue declares Him above every flaw.

outline.heading: Rising from ruku: thanking Him upright
outline.gist: Since no one can thank Allah adequately for all He does, the worshipper rises with back straight and head held high and says Rabbana wa laka al-hamd.

outline.heading: Thanks in rags or in fine clothes before a king
outline.gist: Thanking a king for his generosity while dressed in rags reflects badly on him, while appearing well dressed shows his gift was well placed; standing tall in praise honours Allah's blessings the same way.

outline.heading: Rabi'ah hears the Prophet's long night prayer
outline.gist: Rabi'ah ibn Ka'b, who prepared the Prophet's place for prayer, wanted to pray with him, kept falling asleep, and each time woke to hear him still repeating glorification in ruku and praise after it.

outline.heading: Hold one specific blessing in mind as you praise
outline.gist: When saying 'to You is all praise', choose one blessing, even a single one, and think about it as you say the words.

outline.heading: Rabi'ah is told to ask for anything
outline.gist: Rabi'ah confessed he had grown tired and slept through the Prophet's long standing, and the Prophet invited him to ask for whatever he wished; he weighed asking for something of this world.

outline.heading: Companionship in Paradise and many prostrations
outline.gist: Rabi'ah asked to be with the Prophet in Paradise, and the Prophet told him to help him achieve it through much prostration.

outline.heading: Interlude
Glorifying Allah trains you to accept His decree
outline.gist: Saying Subhan Allah adds nothing to Allah; it coaches the worshipper to affirm that He is holy, flawless and never unjust, preparing him for the hardships of life so he does not object to Allah.

outline.heading: Falling into prostration, the place of dua
outline.gist: After the hadith of the prayer divided between Allah and His servant, he describes the Prophet rising, saying takbir and falling into sujud, and his teaching that bowing is for magnifying Allah while prostration is for abundant dua, likely to be answered.

outline.heading: Record your hopes with Allah in sujud
outline.gist: Tell Allah in prostration where you are heading and what you want to achieve; even if life later pulls you away or you lose the ability to continue, you once placed that hope with Him and it may still come true.

outline.heading: He answers, though not in words
outline.gist: Prayer is the only relationship in which you speak and are answered without words; he recalls how the Prophet spread his arms wide in prostration.

outline.heading: The Prophet's delight in long prostration
outline.gist: The Prophet stayed so long in sujud that companions asked him to ease up, because he was enjoying something most people never taste; dua should not be reduced to getting what one asks for.

outline.heading: A promise to respond, not to grant the request
outline.gist: Allah promised to respond, which may mean removing a hardship, giving something better, giving it later, or keeping it for the moment you need it most; what matters is saying the words and connecting with Him.

outline.heading: Interlude
Outro

2:255.en: Allah! There is no deity save Him, the Alive, the Eternal. Neither slumber nor sleep overtaketh Him. Unto Him belongeth whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is in the earth. Who is he that intercedeth with Him save by His leave? He knoweth that which is in front of them and that which is behind them, while they encompass nothing of His knowledge save what He will. 3:185.ar: كُلُّ نَفۡسࣲ ذَآئِقَةُ ٱلۡمَوۡتِۗ وَإِنَّمَا تُوَفَّوۡنَ أُجُورَكُمۡ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِۖ فَمَن زُحۡزِحَ عَنِ ٱلنَّارِ وَأُدۡخِلَ ٱلۡجَنَّةَ فَقَدۡ فَازَۗ وَمَا ٱلۡحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنۡيَآ إِلَّا مَتَٰعُ ٱلۡغُرُورِ
3:185.en: Every soul will taste of death. And ye will be paid on the Day of Resurrection only that which ye have fairly earned. Whoso is removed from the Fire and is made to enter paradise, he indeed is triumphant. The life of this world is but comfort of illusion

4:78.ar: أَيۡنَمَا تَكُونُواْ يُدۡرِككُّمُ ٱلۡمَوۡتُ وَلَوۡ كُنتُمۡ فِي بُرُوجࣲ مُّشَيَّدَةࣲۗ وَإِن تُصِبۡهُمۡ حَسَنَةࣱ يَقُولُواْ هَٰذِهِۦ مِنۡ عِندِ ٱللَّهِۖ وَإِن تُصِبۡهُمۡ سَيِّئَةࣱ يَقُولُواْ هَٰذِهِۦ مِنۡ عِندِكَۚ قُلۡ كُلࣱّ مِّنۡ عِندِ ٱللَّهِۖ فَمَالِ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ ٱلۡقَوۡمِ لَا يَكَادُونَ يَفۡقَهُونَ حَدِيثࣰ ا
4:78.en: Wheresoever ye may be, death will overtake you, even though ye were in lofty towers. Yet if a happy thing befalleth them they say: This is from Allah; and if an evil thing befalleth them they say: This is of thy doing (O Muhammad). Say (unto them): All is from Allah. What is amiss with these people that they come not nigh to understand a happening

16:61.ar: وَلَوۡ يُؤَاخِذُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلنَّاسَ بِظُلۡمِهِم مَّا تَرَكَ عَلَيۡهَا مِن دَآبَّةࣲ وَلَٰكِن يُؤَخِّرُهُمۡ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلࣲ مُّسَمࣰّ ىۖ فَإِذَا جَآءَ أَجَلُهُمۡ لَا يَسۡتَـٔۡخِرُونَ سَاعَةࣰ وَلَا يَسۡتَقۡدِمُونَ
16:61.en: If Allah were to take mankind to task for their wrong-doing, he would not leave hereon a living creature, but He reprieveth them to an appointed term, and when their term cometh they cannot put (it) off an hour nor (yet) advance (it)

23:99.ar: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَآءَ أَحَدَهُمُ ٱلۡمَوۡتُ قَالَ رَبِّ ٱرۡجِعُونِ
23:99.en: Until, when death cometh unto one of them, he saith: My Lord! Send me back

23:100.ar: لَعَلِّيٓ أَعۡمَلُ صَٰلِحࣰ ا فِيمَا تَرَكۡتُۚ كَلَّآۚ إِنَّهَا كَلِمَةٌ هُوَ قَآئِلُهَاۖ وَمِن وَرَآئِهِم بَرۡزَخٌ إِلَىٰ يَوۡمِ يُبۡعَثُونَ
23:100.en: That I may do right in that which I have left behind! But nay! It is but a word that he speaketh; and behind them is a barrier until the day when they are raised

56:83.en: Why, then, when (the soul) cometh up to the throat (of the dying)

56:84.en: And ye are at that moment looking

56:85.ar: وَنَحۡنُ أَقۡرَبُ إِلَيۡهِ مِنكُمۡ وَلَٰكِن لَّا تُبۡصِرُونَ
56:85.en: And We are nearer unto him than ye are, but ye see not

20:55.ar: ۞مِنۡهَا خَلَقۡنَٰكُمۡ وَفِيهَا نُعِيدُكُمۡ وَمِنۡهَا نُخۡرِجُكُمۡ تَارَةً أُخۡرَىٰ
20:55.en: Thereof We created you, and thereunto We return you, and thence We bring you forth a second time

39:68.ar: وَنُفِخَ فِي ٱلصُّورِ فَصَعِقَ مَن فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَن فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ إِلَّا مَن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُۖ ثُمَّ نُفِخَ فِيهِ أُخۡرَىٰ فَإِذَا هُمۡ قِيَامࣱ يَنظُرُونَ
39:68.en: And the trumpet is blown, and all who are in the heavens and all who are in the earth swoon away, save him whom Allah willeth. Then it is blown a second time, and behold them standing waiting

50:41.ar: وَٱسۡتَمِعۡ يَوۡمَ يُنَادِ ٱلۡمُنَادِ مِن مَّكَانࣲ قَرِيبࣲ‏
50:41.en: And listen on the day when the crier crieth from a near place

50:42.ar: يَوۡمَ يَسۡمَعُونَ ٱلصَّيۡحَةَ بِٱلۡحَقِّۚ ذَٰلِكَ يَوۡمُ ٱلۡخُرُوجِ
50:42.en: The day when they will hear the (Awful) Cry in truth. That is the day of coming forth (from the graves)

22:1.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ ٱتَّقُواْ رَبَّكُمۡۚ إِنَّ زَلۡزَلَةَ ٱلسَّاعَةِ شَيۡءٌ عَظِيمࣱ‏
22:1.en: O mankind! Fear your Lord. Lo! the earthquake of the Hour (of Doom) is a tremendous thing

22:2.ar: يَوۡمَ تَرَوۡنَهَا تَذۡهَلُ كُلُّ مُرۡضِعَةٍ عَمَّآ أَرۡضَعَتۡ وَتَضَعُ كُلُّ ذَاتِ حَمۡلٍ حَمۡلَهَا وَتَرَى ٱلنَّاسَ سُكَٰرَىٰ وَمَا هُم بِسُكَٰرَىٰ وَلَٰكِنَّ عَذَابَ ٱللَّهِ شَدِيدࣱ‏
22:2.en: On the day when ye behold it, every nursing mother will forget her nursling and every pregnant one will be delivered of her burden, and thou (Muhammad) wilt see mankind as drunken, yet they will not be drunken, but the Doom of Allah will be strong (upon them)

54:7.ar: خُشَّعًا أَبۡصَٰرُهُمۡ يَخۡرُجُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡأَجۡدَاثِ كَأَنَّهُمۡ جَرَادࣱ مُّنتَشِرࣱ‏
54:7.en: With downcast eyes, they come forth from the graves as they were locusts spread abroad

54:8.ar: مُّهۡطِعِينَ إِلَى ٱلدَّاعِۖ يَقُولُ ٱلۡكَٰفِرُونَ هَٰذَا يَوۡمٌ عَسِرࣱ‏
54:8.en: Hastening toward the summoner; the disbelievers say: This is a hard day

43:67.ar: ٱلۡأَخِلَّآءُ يَوۡمَئِذِۭ بَعۡضُهُمۡ لِبَعۡضٍ عَدُوٌّ إِلَّا ٱلۡمُتَّقِينَ
43:67.en: Friends on that day will be foes one to another, save those who kept their duty (to Allah)

36:52.ar: قَالُواْ يَٰوَيۡلَنَا مَنۢ بَعَثَنَا مِن مَّرۡقَدِنَاۜۗ هَٰذَا مَا وَعَدَ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنُ وَصَدَقَ ٱلۡمُرۡسَلُونَ
36:52.en: Crying: Woe upon us! Who hath raised us from our place of sleep? This is that which the Beneficent did promise, and the messengers spoke truth

20:105.ar: وَيَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلۡجِبَالِ فَقُلۡ يَنسِفُهَا رَبِّي نَسۡفࣰ ا
20:105.en: They will ask thee of the mountains (on that day). Say: My Lord will break them into scattered dust

23:112.ar: قَٰلَ كَمۡ لَبِثۡتُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ عَدَدَ سِنِينَ
23:112.en: He will say: How long tarried ye in the earth, counting by years

23:113.ar: قَالُواْ لَبِثۡنَا يَوۡمًا أَوۡ بَعۡضَ يَوۡمࣲ فَسۡـَٔلِ ٱلۡعَآدِّينَ
23:113.en: They will say: We tarried by a day or part of a day. Ask of those who keep count

23:114.ar: قَٰلَ إِن لَّبِثۡتُمۡ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣰ اۖ لَّوۡ أَنَّكُمۡ كُنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ
23:114.en: He will say: Ye tarried but a little if ye only knew

70:4.ar: تَعۡرُجُ ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ وَٱلرُّوحُ إِلَيۡهِ فِي يَوۡمࣲ كَانَ مِقۡدَارُهُۥ خَمۡسِينَ أَلۡفَ سَنَةࣲ‏
70:4.en: (Whereby) the angels and the Spirit ascend unto Him in a Day whereof the span is fifty thousand years

69:18.ar: يَوۡمَئِذࣲ تُعۡرَضُونَ لَا تَخۡفَىٰ مِنكُمۡ خَافِيَةࣱ‏
69:18.en: On that day ye will be exposed; not a secret of you will be hidden

40:16.ar: يَوۡمَ هُم بَٰرِزُونَۖ لَا يَخۡفَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ مِنۡهُمۡ شَيۡءࣱۚ لِّمَنِ ٱلۡمُلۡكُ ٱلۡيَوۡمَۖ لِلَّهِ ٱلۡوَٰحِدِ ٱلۡقَهَّارِ
40:16.en: The day when they come forth, nothing of them being hidden from Allah. Whose is the Sovereignty this day? It is Allah's, the One, the Almighty

89:23.ar: وَجِاْيٓءَ يَوۡمَئِذِۭ بِجَهَنَّمَۚ يَوۡمَئِذࣲ يَتَذَكَّرُ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنُ وَأَنَّىٰ لَهُ ٱلذِّكۡرَىٰ
89:23.en: And hell is brought near that day; on that day man will remember, but how will the remembrance (then avail him)

45:28.ar: وَتَرَىٰ كُلَّ أُمَّةࣲ جَاثِيَةࣰۚ كُلُّ أُمَّةࣲ تُدۡعَىٰٓ إِلَىٰ كِتَٰبِهَا ٱلۡيَوۡمَ تُجۡزَوۡنَ مَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ
45:28.en: And thou wilt see each nation crouching, each nation summoned to its record. (And it will be said unto them): This day ye are requited what ye used to do

42:45.ar: وَتَرَىٰهُمۡ يُعۡرَضُونَ عَلَيۡهَا خَٰشِعِينَ مِنَ ٱلذُّلِّ يَنظُرُونَ مِن طَرۡفٍ خَفِيࣲّۗ وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِنَّ ٱلۡخَٰسِرِينَ ٱلَّذِينَ خَسِرُوٓاْ أَنفُسَهُمۡ وَأَهۡلِيهِمۡ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِۗ أَلَآ إِنَّ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ فِي عَذَابࣲ مُّقِيمࣲ‏
42:45.en: And thou wilt see them exposed to (the Fire), made humble by disgrace, and looking with veiled eyes. And those who believe will say: Lo! the (eternal) losers are they who lose themselves and their housefolk on the Day of Resurrection. Lo! are not the wrong-doers in perpetual torment

70:11.ar: يُبَصَّرُونَهُمۡۚ يَوَدُّ ٱلۡمُجۡرِمُ لَوۡ يَفۡتَدِي مِنۡ عَذَابِ يَوۡمِئِذِۭ بِبَنِيهِ
70:11.en: Though they will be given sight of them. The guilty man will long to be able to ransom himself from the punishment of that day at the price of his children

70:12.en: And his spouse and his brother

70:13.en: And his kin that harboured him

70:14.ar: وَمَن فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ جَمِيعࣰ ا ثُمَّ يُنجِيهِ
70:14.en: And all that are in the earth, if then it might deliver him

77:32.en: Lo! it throweth up sparks like the castles

35:37.ar: وَهُمۡ يَصۡطَرِخُونَ فِيهَا رَبَّنَآ أَخۡرِجۡنَا نَعۡمَلۡ صَٰلِحًا غَيۡرَ ٱلَّذِي كُنَّا نَعۡمَلُۚ أَوَلَمۡ نُعَمِّرۡكُم مَّا يَتَذَكَّرُ فِيهِ مَن تَذَكَّرَ وَجَآءَكُمُ ٱلنَّذِيرُۖ فَذُوقُواْ فَمَا لِلظَّٰلِمِينَ مِن نَّصِيرٍ
35:37.en: And they cry for help there, (saying): Our Lord! Release us; we will do right, not (the wrong) that we used to do. Did not We grant you a life long enough for him who reflected to reflect therein? And the warner came unto you. Now taste (the flavour of your deeds), for evil-doers have no helper

81:10.en: And when the pages are laid open

69:19.ar: فَأَمَّا مَنۡ أُوتِيَ كِتَٰبَهُۥ بِيَمِينِهِۦ فَيَقُولُ هَآؤُمُ ٱقۡرَءُواْ كِتَٰبِيَهۡ
69:19.en: Then, as for him who is given his record in his right hand, he will say: Take, read my book

69:25.ar: وَأَمَّا مَنۡ أُوتِيَ كِتَٰبَهُۥ بِشِمَالِهِۦ فَيَقُولُ يَٰلَيۡتَنِي لَمۡ أُوتَ كِتَٰبِيَهۡ
69:25.en: But as for him who is given his record in his left hand, he will say: Oh, would that I had not been given my book

69:26.en: And knew not what my reckoning

69:27.en: Oh, would that it had been death

69:28.en: My wealth hath not availed me

69:29.en: My power hath gone from me

84:10.ar: وَأَمَّا مَنۡ أُوتِيَ كِتَٰبَهُۥ وَرَآءَ ظَهۡرِهِۦ
84:10.en: But whoso is given his account behind his back

68:42.ar: يَوۡمَ يُكۡشَفُ عَن سَاقࣲ وَيُدۡعَوۡنَ إِلَى ٱلسُّجُودِ فَلَا يَسۡتَطِيعُونَ
68:42.en: On the day when it befalleth in earnest, and they are ordered to prostrate themselves but are not able

68:43.ar: خَٰشِعَةً أَبۡصَٰرُهُمۡ تَرۡهَقُهُمۡ ذِلَّةࣱۖ وَقَدۡ كَانُواْ يُدۡعَوۡنَ إِلَى ٱلسُّجُودِ وَهُمۡ سَٰلِمُونَ
68:43.en: With eyes downcast, abasement stupefying them. And they had been summoned to prostrate themselves while they were yet unhurt

19:71.ar: وَإِن مِّنكُمۡ إِلَّا وَارِدُهَاۚ كَانَ عَلَىٰ رَبِّكَ حَتۡمࣰ ا مَّقۡضِيࣰّ ا
19:71.en: There is not one of you but shall approach it. That is a fixed ordinance of thy Lord

57:13.ar: يَوۡمَ يَقُولُ ٱلۡمُنَٰفِقُونَ وَٱلۡمُنَٰفِقَٰتُ لِلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱنظُرُونَا نَقۡتَبِسۡ مِن نُّورِكُمۡ قِيلَ ٱرۡجِعُواْ وَرَآءَكُمۡ فَٱلۡتَمِسُواْ نُورࣰ اۖ فَضُرِبَ بَيۡنَهُم بِسُورࣲ لَّهُۥ بَابُۢ بَاطِنُهُۥ فِيهِ ٱلرَّحۡمَةُ وَظَٰهِرُهُۥ مِن قِبَلِهِ ٱلۡعَذَابُ
57:13.en: On the day when the hypocritical men and the hypocritical women will say unto those who believe: Look on us that we may borrow from your light! it will be said: Go back and seek for light! Then there will separate them a wall wherein is a gate, the inner side whereof containeth mercy, while the outer side thereof is toward the doom

40:17.ar: ٱلۡيَوۡمَ تُجۡزَىٰ كُلُّ نَفۡسِۭ بِمَا كَسَبَتۡۚ لَا ظُلۡمَ ٱلۡيَوۡمَۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَرِيعُ ٱلۡحِسَابِ
40:17.en: This day is each soul requited that which it hath earned; no wrong (is done) this day. Lo! Allah is swift at reckoning

40:18.ar: وَأَنذِرۡهُمۡ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡأٓزِفَةِ إِذِ ٱلۡقُلُوبُ لَدَى ٱلۡحَنَاجِرِ كَٰظِمِينَۚ مَا لِلظَّٰلِمِينَ مِنۡ حَمِيمࣲ وَلَا شَفِيعࣲ يُطَاعُ
40:18.en: Warn them (O Muhammad) of the Day of the approaching (doom), when the hearts will be choking the throats, (when) there will be no friend for the wrong-doers, nor any intercessor who will be heard

18:49.ar: وَوُضِعَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبُ فَتَرَى ٱلۡمُجۡرِمِينَ مُشۡفِقِينَ مِمَّا فِيهِ وَيَقُولُونَ يَٰوَيۡلَتَنَا مَالِ هَٰذَا ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ لَا يُغَادِرُ صَغِيرَةࣰ وَلَا كَبِيرَةً إِلَّآ أَحۡصَىٰهَاۚ وَوَجَدُواْ مَا عَمِلُواْ حَاضِرࣰ اۗ وَلَا يَظۡلِمُ رَبُّكَ أَحَدࣰ ا
18:49.en: And the Book is placed, and thou seest the guilty fearful of that which is therein, and they say: What kind of a Book is this that leaveth not a small thing nor a great thing but hath counted it! And they find all that they did confronting them, and thy Lord wrongeth no-one

J_pcpN4mawk.title: Night 27: Short Reminder and Tawahhum Exercise
J_pcpN4mawk.one_line: A guided tawahhum meditation walking listeners through their own death, grave, resurrection, judgment, the basin, the bridge and Allah's verdict, after a short reminder.
J_pcpN4mawk.summary: After a short reminder by another speaker on keeping Ramadan's gains through reflecting on Allah's names, the brevity of life, the limits of creation and closing the month with istighfar, the sheikh leads tawahhum, an exercise from early third-century scholars. It is not a ritual or a sunnah but a way to picture the known facts of death and the Day of Judgment as happening to you. With the lights dimmed and rounds of la ilaha illa Allah between stages, he narrates in the second person: the angel of death approaching unseen by family, the regrets, the plea to be sent back, the good soul drawn out gently and carried up through the heavens, the wicked soul torn out and thrown down, the loneliness and questions of the grave. Then the first trumpet ending all life, Allah alone asking where the kings are, resurrection, the collapsing cosmos, people gathered naked under a near sun and drowning in sweat, the seven shaded by the Throne, Jahannam dragged in, showing-off reciters and donors thrown in first, books in right or left hands, the call to prostrate, the Prophet's basin, the bridge over the pit, the scales and the final questioning. He ends by asking what in this life is worth hearing Allah's displeasure, reminding listeners the outcome is not yet sealed.

outline.heading: Opening
After Ramadan: will the masjid still be full?
outline.gist: The opening speaker asks whether Ramadan's lessons will be left behind, calling the month a training ground whose real test comes after it.

outline.heading: Reflect on Allah's beautiful names
outline.gist: Studying the names deepens appreciation of Allah; no one has ever been able to take the name Allah for himself.

outline.heading: Al-Hayy and al-Qayyum
outline.gist: The Ever-Living has life with no beginning or end and revives dead hearts; everything depends on the Self-Sustaining.

outline.heading: This life is temporary
outline.gist: Jibril's advice, live as you wish for you will die, shows every pleasure besides Paradise is fleeting.

outline.heading: Limits in creation point to Allah's perfection
outline.gist: Allah placed a limitation in every creature; even angels descend only by His command.

outline.heading: Even the Prophet was wounded and weakened
outline.gist: His wounded face at Uhud and his inability to ask for the miswak on his deathbed show that only Allah's face never changes.

outline.heading: Seal Ramadan with istighfar
outline.gist: Increased deeds invite self-admiration that can waste them; the Prophet sought forgiveness after flawless worship.

outline.heading: Tawahhum: imagining death and judgment as your own
outline.gist: Begun by early third-century scholars, it is an exercise rather than worship: contemplating known facts about death and the Hereafter as happening to you.

outline.heading: Interlude
A creature only you can see approaches
outline.gist: The angel of death comes with companions dressed according to how you lived and sits at arm's length.

outline.heading: Unable to speak as your life replays
outline.gist: Loved ones chat unaware while you remember your choices, mistakes and the amends you never made; every soul tastes death.

outline.heading: Interlude
The angel at your head; hoping for the shahadah
outline.gist: Allah gives respite, but when the time comes nothing changes it; your best hope is to be able to say la ilaha illa Allah.

outline.heading: Interlude
My Lord, send me back: the barzakh begins
outline.gist: The plea to return is refused and a barrier stands until resurrection.

outline.heading: The good and the wicked soul called out
outline.gist: The good soul is named by its best name and flows out like a drop from a spout; the wicked soul hides and is torn out like a branch from wet wool.

outline.heading: The soul at the throat while people sit unaware
outline.gist: Allah and His angels are closer than anyone present; the first stage of the Hereafter begins.

outline.heading: The good soul's ascent through the heavens
outline.gist: Wrapped and perfumed from Paradise, it rises sky by sky, is praised by name, answers Allah truthfully and is returned to the earth.

outline.heading: The wicked soul refused and thrown down
outline.gist: Taken with contempt, its stench remarked on at the gate, it is denied entry, called a liar and cast down to the grave.

outline.heading: Interlude
Alone in the grave: two doors and your deeds
outline.gist: You glimpse both Paradise and Hell before one door closes, and your deeds keep you company, pleasant or terrifying.

outline.heading: The questions of the grave
outline.gist: Who is your Lord, what is your religion, what do you say of the man sent among you; your life decides how easily you answer.

outline.heading: The first trumpet: every living thing dies
outline.gist: It comes like a wave; buyers die before agreeing a price and the spoon never reaches the mouth.

outline.heading: Allah alone: I am the King, where are the kings?
outline.gist: The last angels die at His command and Allah calls on the kings and nobles of the earth, with no one left to answer.

outline.heading: Interlude
The second trumpet and the caller from a near place
outline.gist: Everything that died is brought back to life as the call of truth summons people from their graves.

outline.heading: A day of unprecedented wrath; the great quake
outline.gist: Nursing mothers forget their infants and people stagger as if drunk from fear of Allah's punishment.

outline.heading: Rising from the grave, rebuilt to the fingertips
outline.gist: Your body is reassembled to the last detail and you realize that what you were told was true.

outline.heading: Familiar faces flee; friends become enemies
outline.gist: People scatter like locusts to avoid those they did not worship Allah with; only friendships built on taqwa survive.

outline.heading: Believers calmed; families who worshipped together hold on
outline.gist: Angels reassure the believers that this is the day they prepared for; are you standing with someone or running in shame?

outline.heading: The universe collapses
outline.gist: The sun shrinks, homes and roads vanish, mountains become wool, oceans burn and the heavens are folded in Allah's hand.

outline.heading: Interlude
Naked on a flat white plain
outline.gist: There is nothing to hide behind; people are clothed to different degrees according to their choices.

outline.heading: Driven to the land of judgment
outline.gist: Some ride with dignity, some walk, some are dragged on their faces, some are tiny as ants and trampled.

outline.heading: How long did you stay? A day or part of a day
outline.gist: Even the wisest say they lived a day or less, and Allah confirms it was only a short time.

outline.heading: The sun brought near; drowning in sweat
outline.gist: The day lasts fifty thousand years for some and moments for the obedient; sweat rises from ankles to mouths.

outline.heading: Called to the shade of the Throne
outline.gist: The just leader, the youth raised in worship, the heart attached to the masjid, those who loved for Allah, the one who resisted temptation, the secret giver and the one who wept in private.

outline.heading: Interlude
Exposed as Jahannam is brought
outline.gist: Sins and bodies are uncovered, sovereignty belongs to Allah alone, and people remember when it is too late.

outline.heading: Seventy thousand reins; nations on their knees
outline.gist: Angels drag Jahannam in and hold it back; every nation kneels and steals glances at it in fear.

outline.heading: The first fuel of the Fire: deeds done to be seen
outline.gist: A reciter, a scholar, a fighter and a donor claim they acted for Allah and are told they did it to be praised.

outline.heading: Ransoming everyone to escape
outline.gist: On seeing it people offer their children, spouses, siblings, kin and all of humanity in their place.

outline.heading: Its breath and sparks; did We not give you time?
outline.gist: Its sparks are like castles, kindled for thousands of years; those inside beg to return and are reminded they were warned.

outline.heading: Interlude
The books fly in; the right hand
outline.gist: Records of every life fill the horizon; the fortunate take theirs in the right hand and call others to read it.

outline.heading: The left hand behind the back
outline.gist: The unfortunate hide their left hand, wishing they had never lived and asking where their wealth, status and supporters went.

outline.heading: The procession of the Throne and the angels
outline.gist: Allah's Throne arrives in unmatched majesty, rank after rank of angels moving toward the land of judgment.

outline.heading: The call to prostrate: backs that cannot bend
outline.gist: Those who refused sujud in this life try and cannot, left standing with heads high but no dignity.

outline.heading: Interlude
The Prophet's basin
outline.gist: A familiar, beloved figure at a vast basin of white, musk-scented drink in star-like cups, handing it to those who made the right choices.

outline.heading: Those driven away from the basin
outline.gist: Some are pulled away as the Prophet protests, until he is told how they changed his legacy after him.

outline.heading: Your turn at the basin
outline.gist: Thirsty and anxious, you take the cup from his hand: either you drink and never thirst again, or it is taken away.

outline.heading: Interlude
The edge of the pit: everyone comes to it
outline.gist: A cliff so deep a person falls seventy years; Allah decreed that every person will stand over it.

outline.heading: The bridge and the light you brought
outline.gist: The bridge is a thin rope over darkness; without light you cannot move, and those without it beg others and are told to go back for it.

outline.heading: Crossing: hooks and different speeds
outline.gist: Hooks tear at those crossing; some pass in a blink, like wind or lightning, others crawl and fall before the end.

outline.heading: Interlude
The Prophet's intercession to begin judgment
outline.gist: When judgment is delayed, the Prophet prostrates under the Throne and is told to raise his head and intercede.

outline.heading: The scales and the hundred mercies
outline.gist: Every person's deeds are weighed; Allah adds the one mercy of this world to the ninety-nine and spreads them over creation.

outline.heading: Reading your book, waiting for your name
outline.gist: Your claim of la ilaha illa Allah is only as valid as your deeds allow; some go joyfully, others are taken in tears.

outline.heading: Before Allah: concealed or exposed
outline.gist: The fortunate are covered and concealed; others are judged publicly while people curse a book that leaves nothing out.

outline.heading: Questioned about your wealth, time and youth
outline.gist: The detailed questioning is unanswerable, since no one can explain living unprepared for this moment.

outline.heading: I am pleased with you, or the opposite
outline.gist: Allah's pleasure erases every pain and trauma forever; His wrath is the outcome to fear.

outline.heading: You are still here: the outcome is not sealed
outline.gist: Nothing in this life is worth Allah's displeasure; you can still choose, by embracing and living la ilaha illa Allah.

outline.heading: Outro

G-nz6qN2POU.title: Ramadan 2025, Night 28: Accountability
G-nz6qN2POU.one_line: Accountability as Ramadan's goal: souls held hostage by their deeds, recompense that fits the deed, and those who forget they will be raised.
G-nz6qN2POU.summary: He ties mortality, resurrection and accountability into one package: people find comfort in coming back, but the real concern is being questioned about what they did with their freedom, which ends at death. Life now offers choice with little accountability; then there is none of the first and all of the second. Living with that concern is the way to be spared it, as in the hadith qudsi that Allah never gives His servant two fears or two securities. From Al-Muddaththir 74:38-47 he explains that every soul is held hostage by what it earned except the people of the right, and that those in Saqar admit they neither prayed, fed the poor, nor did more than follow the crowd. From An-Naba 78:26 he shows that recompense mirrors the deed: Khadijah, who climbed to the cave and ran a loud household, was promised a hollow palace free of noise and fatigue, and Ibrahim reclines against the House he built. Yet we pray every night hoping not to be paid merely according to our deeds, but with mercy. From Al-Mutaffifin 83:1-6 he links double standards to the killing in Gaza and asks whether its perpetrators think they will not be raised. He urges everyone to have at least an honest answer: I tried.

outline.heading: Opening
Praying that London keeps one Eid
outline.gist: In over twelve years the large London masjids have never split on Eid; he asks for dua that neighbours do not break their fast on different days.

outline.heading: Mortality, accountability and resurrection as one package
outline.gist: Accepting death means accepting accountability and resurrection; Muslims take all three together while others accept only parts.

outline.heading: In a hundred years every face here will be gone
outline.gist: We fall like dominoes one after another, and attached to that certainty is the certainty of being questioned.

outline.heading: Coming back is comforting; the questions are not
outline.gist: Resurrection eases the fear of death, but Allah will ask how we used what He gave us and the choices we made.

outline.heading: Losing the margin of freedom
outline.gist: On that day you cannot sit, speak or object; even small losses of freedom hurt, and then most of it is gone.

outline.heading: Now: anything can become a blessing
outline.gist: In this life whatever Allah sends can be turned into good through patience or gratitude; nothing is punishment unless you make it so.

outline.heading: You are the sole author of your story
outline.gist: Everything is recorded, and you will have to explain why the hero of your story made the choices he did.

outline.heading: Worry about accountability to be spared it
outline.gist: Hoping to enter paradise without reckoning requires living with accountability as your main concern.

outline.heading: Two fears or two securities
outline.gist: Allah does not give His servant two fears or two securities: fear Him in this world and be safe on the Day of Gathering.

outline.heading: What Ramadan should have built
outline.gist: The month should have strengthened in the heart the readiness to be held accountable.

outline.heading: Ignoring accountability explains poor choices
outline.gist: Someone who expects to be questioned decides differently; Muslims who act without wisdom have put accountability in their blind spot.

outline.heading: Every soul is held hostage
outline.gist: Rahinah means hostage: your deeds hold you until they release you, and paradise was created for everyone who is released.

outline.heading: What a soul earned is broader than deeds
outline.gist: Kasb covers intentions, hopes and what you did or left undone, not only actions.

outline.heading: The exception: the people of the right
outline.gist: Wherever the Quran speaks of being repaid by deeds, it excepts Allah's chosen servants, whose mistakes He erases; they ask about the criminals from their gardens.

outline.heading: What brought you into Saqar?
outline.gist: The people of the Fire admit they did not pray and did not feed the poor.

outline.heading: Going with the flow, and coming alone
outline.gist: They followed whatever was popular and hid among the crowd, but everyone stands alone before Allah without friends or family.

outline.heading: Denying the Day of Debt
outline.gist: Yawm ad-din is the day debts fall due, paid in full at once; whoever cannot pay remains a hostage.

outline.heading: An-Naba: the news according to Allah
outline.gist: Amid all the news outlets and messages we receive, this surah gives the news that matters, from creation to recompense.

outline.heading: A recompense that fits the deed
outline.gist: What you are given will come from the essence of what you did.

outline.heading: Jibril brings salam to the dying Khadijah
outline.gist: After standing by the Prophet for twenty-five years and through the boycott that broke her health, she received Allah's greeting and answered that Allah is As-Salam.

outline.heading: A palace of hollow pearl
outline.gist: She was promised a house of hollow pearl in paradise with no noise and no fatigue, and passed away that night.

outline.heading: A reward shaped like the cave she climbed to
outline.gist: The hollow palace resembles the cave of Hira where she carried food to him and supported his retreats; without her support the story would have been different.

outline.heading: Quiet for a woman who ran a loud house
outline.gist: Her home was full of children and relatives, so her reward is rest without noise or tiredness.

outline.heading: Ibrahim reclining against the House
outline.gist: In the Ascension the Prophet saw Ibrahim leaning on the Bayt al-Ma'mur, a reward matching the toil of settling his family in Mecca and building the Kaaba.

outline.heading: No less than deserved; more is Allah's choice
outline.gist: Recompense is exact, never less; any increase is Allah's gift, and our merchandise is poor.

outline.heading: Why we stand every night
outline.gist: Aching feet and backs in taraweeh are a plea that Allah multiply and purify our deeds rather than pay us their worth.

outline.heading: I have no argument, only His mercy
outline.gist: We will come admitting we have nothing worth showing, which is the source of humility and sincerity.

outline.heading: The examiner decides who passes
outline.gist: As he can make an oral exam easy or impossible for a student, Allah can ease the reckoning, so come to Him humbly.

outline.heading: Al-Mutaffifin: double standards on the scale
outline.gist: They take their full rights and rig the scales when it is time to give others theirs.

outline.heading: Gaza and a world of double standards
outline.gist: Seventeen months of bombing residential areas and children pulled from rubble can only be explained by people who do not see others as equal; one unjust killing outweighs the world.

outline.heading: Do they not think they will be raised?
outline.gist: Allah asks whether such people do not expect resurrection on a tremendous day when everyone stands before the Lord of the worlds.

outline.heading: At least be able to say 'I tried'
outline.gist: We will be asked about our time, wealth, youth and goals; even with failures, show Allah you truly wanted to be His dedicated servant.

outline.heading: Ramadan reminds us to come humbly
outline.gist: Accountability means coming before Allah humbly, begging for mercy and hoping something we did earns His praise.

outline.heading: Interlude
Civic engagement as part of accountability
outline.gist: Applying political pressure is a tool Muslims have; choosing not to use it and then complaining is something we will answer for, and small differences add up.

outline.heading: Outro

cjNl1SEe3OI.one_line: A recap of the whole tazkiyah path: its three goals, the practical steps, the fruits in the heart, and why it is a lifelong path.
cjNl1SEe3OI.summary: He sums up tazkiyah's goals as clarity, closeness to Allah and control over oneself, reachable only by following the Quran and Sunnah in detail. He explains why twenty sessions focused on foundations rather than spiritual highs: emotions are the heart's output, and arrogance or low self-esteem are feelings produced by wrong inputs, so the work is protecting and purifying the heart, which grows more sensitive the more it is cared for. He then retraces the practical path: applying everything to yourself, daily Quran and dhikr, spiritual exercises, contemplation, the four daily focuses, gradual change, and the cycle of thoughts, actions and emotions. Its fruits are stable self-value, humility that removes vanity, envy and ostentation, sincerity, compassion, acceptance of death, tools for facing life, and finally genuine love. He contrasts this with cults that keep the goal forever out of reach: in Islam real progress is possible, but closeness to Allah is endless, so it is a path rather than an arrival. Stay aware of your flaws and never give up, especially after Ramadan when the devils return. Stories of Junayd as a boy and Ibn Taymiyyah's inner paradise illustrate fulfilment. He asks listeners to revisit the series and practise patiently, since gradual change is hard to see.

outline.heading: Opening
The three goals: clarity, closeness, control
outline.gist: Tazkiyah brings clarity of mind and intention, enjoyment of closeness to Allah, and control that yields consistency in ethics.

outline.heading: Only through the Quran and Sunnah
outline.gist: There is no tazkiyah outside close adherence to the Quran and the Prophet's example, living with patience in hardship and gratitude in ease.

outline.heading: Why foundations, not spiritual highs
outline.gist: Tears and spiritual highs are results; without the core values in place they cannot occur, so the series focused on the formula.

outline.heading: Emotions are the heart's output
outline.gist: Feelings are our most real experiences; arrogance and low self-esteem are emotions produced by wrong beliefs and comparisons, which is why they are hard to shake.

outline.heading: Protecting the heart's mixing pot
outline.gist: Tazkiyah keeps Shaytan out of the heart, purifies its ingredients and lets Allah's light in; a cared-for heart becomes more sensitive to what we see, hear and whom we sit with.

outline.heading: The practical path retraced
outline.gist: Apply everything to yourself, keep daily Quran and dhikr, do spiritual exercises, contemplate daily, hold the four focuses, accept gradual change and use the cycle of thoughts, actions and emotions.

outline.heading: Fruits: stable self-value and humility
outline.gist: Slowly self-value solidifies and humility drives out vanity, arrogance, envy and ostentation; anger, distraction and greed decline.

outline.heading: Fruits: sincerity, reverence, repentance, compassion
outline.gist: Worship becomes for Allah alone, reverence grows, reflection on values activates tawbah, and compassion strengthens humility.

outline.heading: Accepting mortality
outline.gist: Death becomes Allah calling you home and every hardship a chance to prove yourself; fear and denial of death fade.

outline.heading: Tools for facing life
outline.gist: With stable self-value and acceptance of death, tools like reliance, patience and striving become usable, and living like the companions feels possible.

outline.heading: A cleansed heart and a tamed nafs
outline.gist: Conscience gains a say, the nafs becomes better behaved, and the heart is scraped clean and protected from Shaytan and desire.

outline.heading: The culmination: genuine love
outline.gist: A purified heart generates genuine love, free of control, obsession or need, and with it you have found everything.

outline.heading: The thin line between growth and cults
outline.gist: Cults keep moving the goal so followers stay dependent; tazkiyah lets you truly attain something if you commit with grit and a good teacher.

outline.heading: A path, not a destination
outline.gist: There is no final arrival; closeness to Allah is infinite, so you can always be a little closer, or further.

outline.heading: Keep trying despite imperfection
outline.gist: As long as you stay aware of your flaws, hold yourself accountable and get up after each fall, you are safe; danger lies in giving up.

outline.heading: Shaytan waits for you to lower your guard
outline.gist: Once Ramadan ends the devils are released and head straight for the hearts that were lit up, looking for holes to poison the mix.

outline.heading: Walk this path until you die
outline.gist: If you know a shortcoming is wrong and you care, keep pushing and never give up.

outline.heading: Junayd as a boy on gratitude
outline.gist: Asked about shukr, the child answered that it means not disobeying Allah with His blessings; his teacher feared his share from Allah would be only his tongue, words he wept over for sixty years.

outline.heading: Ibn Taymiyyah: my paradise is in my chest
outline.gist: Threatened with prison, he said exile would be travel, prison a retreat with Allah and death martyrdom, so his enemies held nothing over him.

outline.heading: The fulfilment of one who loves Allah
outline.gist: Someone with Allah's love in his heart is happy whether rich or poor, sick or well, and spends life protecting it.

outline.heading: Listen again and practise
outline.gist: Hearing the ideas changes nothing on its own; reflect, practise and incorporate them until they become second nature.

outline.heading: Gradual change is hard to see
outline.gist: Students who feel nothing changed in two years see real progress when they compare themselves with who they were.

outline.heading: The rare souls Allah draws to Himself
outline.gist: A few people are drawn by Allah without the long path, humble and full of love with little knowledge; the rest of us must work and ask Him.

2:286.ar: لَا يُكَلِّفُ ٱللَّهُ نَفۡسًا إِلَّا وُسۡعَهَاۚ لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتۡ وَعَلَيۡهَا مَا ٱكۡتَسَبَتۡۗ رَبَّنَا لَا تُؤَاخِذۡنَآ إِن نَّسِينَآ أَوۡ أَخۡطَأۡنَاۚ رَبَّنَا وَلَا تَحۡمِلۡ عَلَيۡنَآ إِصۡرࣰ ا كَمَا حَمَلۡتَهُۥ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِنَاۚ رَبَّنَا وَلَا تُحَمِّلۡنَا مَا لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا بِهِۦۖ وَٱعۡفُ عَنَّا وَٱغۡفِرۡ لَنَا وَٱرۡحَمۡنَآۚ أَنتَ مَوۡلَىٰنَا فَٱنصُرۡنَا عَلَى ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
2:286.en: Allah tasketh not a soul beyond its scope. For it (is only) that which it hath earned, and against it (only) that which it hath deserved. Our Lord! Condemn us not if we forget, or miss the mark! Our Lord! Lay not on us such a burden as thou didst lay on those before us! Our Lord! Impose not on us that which we have not the strength to bear! Pardon us, absolve us and have mercy on us, Thou, our Protector, and give us victory over the disbelieving folk

4:48.ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَغۡفِرُ أَن يُشۡرَكَ بِهِۦ وَيَغۡفِرُ مَا دُونَ ذَٰلِكَ لِمَن يَشَآءُۚ وَمَن يُشۡرِكۡ بِٱللَّهِ فَقَدِ ٱفۡتَرَىٰٓ إِثۡمًا عَظِيمًا
4:48.en: Lo! Allah forgiveth not that a partner should be ascribed unto Him. He forgiveth (all) save that to whom He will. Whoso ascribeth partners to Allah, he hath indeed invented a tremendous sin

4:116.ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَغۡفِرُ أَن يُشۡرَكَ بِهِۦ وَيَغۡفِرُ مَا دُونَ ذَٰلِكَ لِمَن يَشَآءُۚ وَمَن يُشۡرِكۡ بِٱللَّهِ فَقَدۡ ضَلَّ ضَلَٰلَۢا بَعِيدًا
4:116.en: Lo! Allah pardoneth not that partners should be ascribed unto Him. He pardoneth all save that to whom He will. Whoso ascribeth partners unto Allah hath wandered far astray

42:25.ar: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي يَقۡبَلُ ٱلتَّوۡبَةَ عَنۡ عِبَادِهِۦ وَيَعۡفُواْ عَنِ ٱلسَّيِّـَٔاتِ وَيَعۡلَمُ مَا تَفۡعَلُونَ
42:25.en: And He it is Who accepteth repentance from His bondmen, and pardoneth the evil deeds, and knoweth what ye do

35:6.ar: إِنَّ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنَ لَكُمۡ عَدُوࣱّ فَٱتَّخِذُوهُ عَدُوًّاۚ إِنَّمَا يَدۡعُواْ حِزۡبَهُۥ لِيَكُونُواْ مِنۡ أَصۡحَٰبِ ٱلسَّعِيرِ
35:6.en: Lo! the devil is an enemy for you, so treat him as an enemy. He only summoneth his faction to be owners of the flaming Fire

2:37.ar: فَتَلَقَّىٰٓ ءَادَمُ مِن رَّبِّهِۦ كَلِمَٰتࣲ فَتَابَ عَلَيۡهِۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
2:37.en: Then Adam received from his Lord words (of revelation), and He relented toward him. Lo! He is the relenting, the Merciful

25:68.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَدۡعُونَ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَٰهًا ءَاخَرَ وَلَا يَقۡتُلُونَ ٱلنَّفۡسَ ٱلَّتِي حَرَّمَ ٱللَّهُ إِلَّا بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَلَا يَزۡنُونَۚ وَمَن يَفۡعَلۡ ذَٰلِكَ يَلۡقَ أَثَامࣰ ا
25:68.en: And those who cry not unto any other god along with Allah, nor take the life which Allah hath forbidden save in (course of) justice, nor commit adultery - and whoso doeth this shall pay the penalty

25:69.ar: يُضَٰعَفۡ لَهُ ٱلۡعَذَابُ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ وَيَخۡلُدۡ فِيهِۦ مُهَانًا
25:69.en: The doom will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein disdained for ever

25:70.ar: إِلَّا مَن تَابَ وَءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ عَمَلࣰ ا صَٰلِحࣰ ا فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ يُبَدِّلُ ٱللَّهُ سَيِّـَٔاتِهِمۡ حَسَنَٰتࣲۗ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ غَفُورࣰ ا رَّحِيمࣰ ا
25:70.en: Save him who repenteth and believeth and doth righteous work; as for such, Allah will change their evil deeds to good deeds. Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful

39:53.ar: ۞قُلۡ يَٰعِبَادِيَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَسۡرَفُواْ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمۡ لَا تَقۡنَطُواْ مِن رَّحۡمَةِ ٱللَّهِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَغۡفِرُ ٱلذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعًاۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلۡغَفُورُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
39:53.en: Say: O My slaves who have been prodigal to their own hurt! Despair not of the mercy of Allah, Who forgiveth all sins. Lo! He is the Forgiving, the Merciful

2:222.ar: وَيَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلۡمَحِيضِۖ قُلۡ هُوَ أَذࣰ ى فَٱعۡتَزِلُواْ ٱلنِّسَآءَ فِي ٱلۡمَحِيضِ وَلَا تَقۡرَبُوهُنَّ حَتَّىٰ يَطۡهُرۡنَۖ فَإِذَا تَطَهَّرۡنَ فَأۡتُوهُنَّ مِنۡ حَيۡثُ أَمَرَكُمُ ٱللَّهُۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلتَّوَّٰبِينَ وَيُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُتَطَهِّرِينَ
2:222.en: They question thee (O Muhammad) concerning menstruation. Say: It is an illness, so let women alone at such times and go not in unto them till they are cleansed. And when they have purified themselves, then go in unto them as Allah hath enjoined upon you. Truly Allah loveth those who turn unto Him, and loveth those who have a care for cleanness

24:22.ar: وَلَا يَأۡتَلِ أُوْلُواْ ٱلۡفَضۡلِ مِنكُمۡ وَٱلسَّعَةِ أَن يُؤۡتُوٓاْ أُوْلِي ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَٱلۡمَسَٰكِينَ وَٱلۡمُهَٰجِرِينَ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِۖ وَلۡيَعۡفُواْ وَلۡيَصۡفَحُوٓاْۗ أَلَا تُحِبُّونَ أَن يَغۡفِرَ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمٌ
24:22.en: And let not those who possess dignity and ease among you swear not to give to the near of kin and to the needy, and to fugitives for the cause of Allah. Let them forgive and show indulgence. Yearn ye not that Allah may forgive you? Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

3:133.ar: ۞وَسَارِعُوٓاْ إِلَىٰ مَغۡفِرَةࣲ مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡ وَجَنَّةٍ عَرۡضُهَا ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتُ وَٱلۡأَرۡضُ أُعِدَّتۡ لِلۡمُتَّقِينَ
3:133.en: And vie one with another for forgiveness from your Lord, and for a paradise as wide as are the heavens and the earth, prepared for those who ward off (evil)

57:21.ar: سَابِقُوٓاْ إِلَىٰ مَغۡفِرَةࣲ مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡ وَجَنَّةٍ عَرۡضُهَا كَعَرۡضِ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ أُعِدَّتۡ لِلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ بِٱللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِۦۚ ذَٰلِكَ فَضۡلُ ٱللَّهِ يُؤۡتِيهِ مَن يَشَآءُۚ وَٱللَّهُ ذُو ٱلۡفَضۡلِ ٱلۡعَظِيمِ
57:21.en: Race one with another for forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden whereof the breadth is as the breadth of the heavens and the earth, which is in store for those who believe in Allah and His messengers. Such is the bounty of Allah, which He bestoweth upon whom He will, and Allah is of Infinite Bounty

uNgSzUtw2sU.title: Ramadan 2025, Night 27: Tawbah and Forgiveness
uNgSzUtw2sU.one_line: Why seeking forgiveness is urgent, what al-Ghaffar and at-Tawwab mean, the conditions of tawbah, and forgiving others as Allah forgives us.
uNgSzUtw2sU.summary: The talk opens with the man who killed a hundred people and was still forgiven, drawing out that Allah reshaped the very earth to accept a sincere penitent and that forgiveness has two sides, with Allah and with people. Because every human errs and death can come at any moment, seeking forgiveness is urgent, and Ramadan is the season for it after months of distraction. The speaker explains al-Ghafur and al-Ghaffar through the root meaning of covering, Ibn Kathir's distinction between pardon, concealment and mercy, and the blessing that our sins are hidden from others. Every sin can be forgiven except dying upon shirk. Istighfar is distinguished from tawbah, which is for a sin one keeps returning to, and at-Tawwab is presented as the One who both accepts the return and inspires it. Using Adam, the verses of al-Furqan and the example of Umar, the conditions are set out: stop the sin, regret it from the heart, and change the deeds and surroundings that feed it. No one should despair, since Allah runs toward the one who walks to Him. The talk closes with Abu Bakr forgiving Mistah and asks listeners to drop grudges and never reopen an apology once accepted.

outline.heading: Opening
The man who killed a hundred
outline.gist: A man who had killed 99 asks a monk whether he can repent, is told no and kills him too; a scholar then tells him nothing stands between him and repentance and sends him to a land of worshippers, and he dies on the way.

outline.heading: Allah reshapes the earth for a penitent
outline.gist: The angels of mercy and punishment dispute over him and the land is measured in his favour; Allah bent the order of the earth to accept a man who kept seeking, and forgiveness has a side with Allah and a side with people.

outline.heading: Why forgiveness is urgent
outline.gist: Every child of Adam errs whether he admits it or not, and all will be held accountable; since no one knows whether death comes tomorrow or within the hour, seeking forgiveness cannot wait.

outline.heading: Ramadan as the season of return
outline.gist: The door of forgiveness stays open until death, and after eleven months of distraction Ramadan raises consciousness of Allah and is the time to free ourselves through His forgiveness.

outline.heading: Al-Ghafur, al-Ghaffar: forgiveness as covering
outline.gist: The root means to cover, as one covers hot food or covers a body in the earth; Allah conceals the sin so no one knows of it and removes its punishment.

outline.heading: An earth full of sins, met with forgiveness
outline.gist: In a hadith qudsi, whoever calls on Allah and hopes in Him without associating partners is met with forgiveness as vast as the sins he brings.

outline.heading: Pardon, concealment and mercy
outline.gist: Ibn Kathir reads the closing dua of al-Baqarah as pardon between you and Allah, covering before people, and mercy that protects you in the future; imagine if our sins had a smell or were known to all, we would never leave our homes.

outline.heading: Every sin but shirk
outline.gist: Allah forgives anything below associating partners with Him for whom He wills, so only dying upon shirk closes the door.

outline.heading: Istighfar versus tawbah
outline.gist: Istighfar is for general mistakes and shortcomings, while tawbah is needed for a sin one keeps committing again and again.

outline.heading: At-Tawwab: the One who inspires the return
outline.gist: Tawbah is turning back to the right direction; linguists add that at-Tawwab also means Allah moves you to come back, so the unease that pushes a struggling sinner back to Him is itself His mercy.

outline.heading: At-Tawwab paired with al-Hakim and ar-Rahim
outline.gist: The name comes eleven times in the Quran, once with al-Hakim, since He accepts repentance with a wisdom we cannot see, and ten times with ar-Rahim.

outline.heading: A clean slate, unlike with people
outline.gist: After a fight with a person there is lingering awkwardness, but when you return to Allah you start completely clean; He accepts repentance from His servants and pardons misdeeds.

outline.heading: Adam's slip and the words of return
outline.gist: Shaytan is an open enemy, Adam ate from the tree and was sent down not knowing how to come back, and Allah gave him words with which He turned to him.

outline.heading: The gravest sins and the great exception
outline.gist: Al-Furqan lists shirk, killing and zina with a multiplied, lasting punishment, then exempts whoever repents, believes and does good, whose bad deeds Allah turns into good ones.

outline.heading: Condition: leaving the sin
outline.gist: Repentance cannot be real while you are still actively committing the sin.

outline.heading: Condition: genuine regret
outline.gist: You must recognise and believe deep in your heart that what you did was wrong, as when one looks back on one's younger days with real remorse.

outline.heading: Condition: action and a changed environment
outline.gist: Quitting while returning to the same places and friends leads straight back into the sin; righteous deeds and removing what pulls you back are part of tawbah, including the rights of Allah and of people.

outline.heading: Umar: from a date idol to a restrained ruler
outline.gist: Umar once made an idol of dates and ate it when hungry, yet decades later, accused of injustice and reddening with anger, he held back when reminded; real repentance shows in changed behaviour.

outline.heading: Never despair of Allah's mercy
outline.gist: Great companions spent years in shirk before Islam; whoever feels too burdened to be forgiven should hear Allah call those who wronged themselves not to despair, for He forgives all sins.

outline.heading: Walk to Him and He comes running
outline.gist: The more effort one makes the more one receives: Allah draws an arm's length nearer for a hand-span and runs to the one who walks, and He loves those who repent and purify themselves.

outline.heading: Repair after repentance
outline.gist: Tawbah is followed by setting things right, and Allah turns bad deeds into good; Khalid ibn al-Walid, once an enemy, shows how far a person can be transformed.

outline.heading: Abu Bakr forgives Mistah
outline.gist: When a relative he supported joined the slander against Aisha, Abu Bakr swore to cut him off, and Allah asked: do you not love that Allah forgives you? He resumed his support.

outline.heading: The grudges we hold
outline.gist: A friend repays a loan a week late or wrongs us once, and we keep reminding them of what we did for them; if we need Allah's forgiveness we must give it to others.

outline.heading: Race toward forgiveness
outline.gist: Two verses urge hastening to forgiveness from your Lord and a garden as wide as the heavens and earth, prepared for the God-conscious and for those who believe in Allah and His messengers.

outline.heading: The last nights: forgive as you want to be forgiven
outline.gist: Ramadan is nearly over, so make the most of the remaining days; keep an easy heart with people, and once someone apologises and changes, never bring it up again.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Hope, fear and the balance between them
themes.note: The threat attached to the gravest sins is balanced by the exception for the penitent and the command never to despair of Allah's mercy.

themes.label: Mercy, forgiveness and pardoning people
themes.note: Abu Bakr's forgiveness of Mistah and everyday grudges: whoever wants Allah's forgiveness must forgive others and not reopen an accepted apology.

themes.label: Ramadan: preparation, fasting, making the most of it
themes.note: Ramadan is the season to seek forgiveness after a year of distraction.

themes.label: Ramadan: preparation, fasting, making the most of it
themes.note: Use the last nights to seek forgiveness and to forgive.

themes.label: Mortality, death and preparing for it
themes.note: No one knows when death comes, which makes seeking forgiveness urgent.

themes.label: The companions and the early generations
themes.note: Umar, Khalid and Abu Bakr as examples of transformation after shirk and of forgiving those who wrong you.

quran.point: Pardon us, forgive us, have mercy on us, read through Ibn Kathir as three distinct requests
Allah forgives everything except associating partners with Him
The parallel verse ending with straying far astray
Allah accepts repentance from His servants and pardons misdeeds
Shaytan is an enemy, so take him as one
Adam received words from his Lord and Allah turned to him
Shirk, killing and zina bring a multiplied, lasting punishment
Whoever repents, believes and does good has his bad deeds turned into good
Do not despair of Allah's mercy; He forgives all sins
Allah loves those who repent and purify themselves
Revealed about Abu Bakr and Mistah: pardon and overlook, do you not love that Allah forgives you
Hasten to forgiveness and a garden as wide as the heavens and earth
Race toward forgiveness and a garden prepared for those who believe

hadith.gist: A man who killed ninety-nine, then a hundred, sets out to repent, dies on the way, and the angels measure the land in his favour
Every child of Adam errs, and the best of those who err are those who repent
Hadith qudsi: as long as you call on Me and hope in Me without associating partners, I forgive you; bring an earth full of sins and I bring as much forgiveness
Hadith qudsi: whoever draws near a hand-span, Allah draws near an arm's length; whoever comes walking, He comes running

maxims: Once they apologise, never bring it up again

stories.who: The man who killed a hundred people
stories.point: No sin is beyond forgiveness for one who keeps seeking; Allah even shifted the earth to accept him.

stories.who: Adam
stories.point: After his slip Allah Himself taught him how to return.

stories.who: Umar ibn al-Khattab
stories.point: The man who once ate his own date idol became a ruler who restrained his anger when reminded; repentance shows in changed behaviour.

stories.who: Abu Bakr and Mistah
stories.point: He forgave a relative who joined the slander against Aisha because he wanted Allah's forgiveness for himself.

takeaways: Seek forgiveness now rather than later, since no one knows when death comes.
Make tawbah complete: stop the sin, regret it sincerely, and change the friends and places that pull you back.
Never despair over the size of a sin; take a step toward Allah and He comes closer.
Use the last nights of Ramadan to seek forgiveness.
Forgive those who wronged you, and once they apologise do not raise it again.
